title: U.S. House · Pennsylvania's 4th District
area: Parts of Montgomery and Berks counties.

context.text: Madeleine Dean advanced from the Democratic primary unopposed. Aurora Stuski won the Republican primary unopposed.

summary.text: Madeleine Dean is the Democratic incumbent, in the U.S. House since 2019. A former lawyer, college writing and ethics instructor and columnist, she served as an Abington Township commissioner and in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives from 2012 to 2018 before winning the 4th District seat in 2018. In the 119th Congress (2025-2026) she serves on the House Appropriations and House Foreign Affairs committees.

background.text: Born in 1959 and raised in Glenside, Pennsylvania, with five older brothers and one older sister; graduated from Abington High School and, at age 18, won election as a local committeeperson.
Earned a B.A. in English language and literature from La Salle University (1981) and a J.D. from Widener University School of Law (1984).
Practiced law in a small Philadelphia firm and with the Philadelphia Trial Lawyers Association, where she became executive director, then opened a small law practice in Glenside.

From 2001 to 2011 was a member of La Salle University's English Department, teaching writing and ethics, and contributed columns to The Philadelphia Inquirer, the Daily News, The Patriot-News and other publications.

After studying politics and public service at the University of Pennsylvania's Fels School of Government, was elected an Abington Township commissioner in 2011 and won a special election to the Pennsylvania House of Representatives (District 153) in 2012, serving until 2018.

In the Pennsylvania House, founded and co-chaired the PA-SAFE Caucus, a coalition of legislators and advocates focused on gun violence; in 2015 Gov. Tom Wolf appointed her to the Pennsylvania Commission for Women.

Won election to the U.S. House in 2018 for the 4th District, at a time when, her official biography notes, Pennsylvania's 18-member House delegation included no women; in the 118th Congress served on the Judiciary Committee (vice chair in 2021-2022) and the Foreign Affairs Committee.
Serves in her fourth term on the House Appropriations and House Foreign Affairs committees. Her official biography says she is married to PJ Cunnane and they have three sons and seven grandchildren.

positions.summary: Her official site says reproductive healthcare is a fundamental right and that she cosponsored the Women’s Health Protection Act of 2021.
positions.quote: Rep. Dean unequivocally supports women and their right to make intimate medical decisions in consultation with their doctors.

positions.summary: Her official site describes her as supporting universal, affordable healthcare, defending the ACA and Medicaid expansion, and making the enhanced ACA premium subsidies permanent.
positions.quote: Rep. Dean supports universal, affordable high-quality healthcare.

positions.summary: Her official site describes her work for universal background checks (H.R. 8), the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act and limits on undetectable firearms.
positions.quote: Rep. Dean also championed the first meaningful gun violence prevention legislation in nearly 30 years

positions.summary: Her official site says she supports legislation to boost investment in renewable energy and cosponsored the Climate Action Now Act and a carbon-fee bill aiming for net zero emissions by 2050.
positions.quote: Rep. Dean supports legislation to boost America’s investments in renewable energy, fund green infrastructure, and reengage in global agreements to combat climate change.

record.text: Reintroduced legislation to protect children from gun violence and introduced the Gun Violence Prevention Through Financial Intelligence Act with colleagues.
Reintroduced a bill with Sen. Gillibrand to empower victims of significant PFAS exposure to sue manufacturers.
Celebrated the first national standard to limit PFAS pollution in drinking water.
Voted for the CHIPS and Science Act, which she said would lower families' costs and boost American manufacturing.

candidates.name: Aurora Stuski
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19, 2026 Republican primary unopposed.

summary.text: Aurora Stuski is a West Norriton, Montgomery County business owner running as the Republican nominee. She is the founder and owner of AAS Appraisal Lab, a jewelry and collectibles appraisal business, and has held local Republican Party roles since 2022. According to her campaign website, her platform centers on limited government, lower taxes on homeowners, and community safety.

background.text: According to her campaign website, grew up in Philadelphia and moved to West Norriton, Montgomery County, in 1987, where she has lived for more than 35 years and raised three children.
Her campaign website lists a Bachelor of Fine Arts from Arcadia University with a minor in business administration, and a Graduate Gemologist credential from the Gemological Institute of America.
Earlier in her career worked in the architectural field on proposal development and accounts receivable for a national firm that builds hospitals and healthcare facilities.

Founder and owner of AAS Appraisal Lab, serving Montgomery County since 1989, offering appraisals of jewelry, coins and collectibles, expert witness testimony, estate valuation and insurance claim arbitration.
Her campaign site says she volunteered on Ernie Preate's 1989-1995 Attorney General campaign and on Kathy Barnette's congressional and Senate campaigns in 2019-2021.

Her campaign site lists her party roles as West Norriton Republican Committee chair and Montgomery County Republican Committee Area 8 vice chair (both 2024-present), West Norriton committee person (2022-present), and an elected delegate to the Republican National Convention from the 4th District; it also lists past runs for county commissioner and West Norriton commissioner.
Serves as a board member of West Norriton United, a community civic organization.

priorities.text: Campaign focuses on "safe communities, a stronger economy, secure borders, and government that answers to the people again."
Says she is focused on reducing the tax burden on homeowners, protecting seniors from being forced out of their homes, and preserving green space in West Norriton.

statements.quote: I do not condone much of what has happened in Gaza, and I believe the United States must carefully evaluate how its financial assistance, weapons transfers, and diplomatic support are being used.

Any proposed deployment should have a clear mission, a lawful basis, appropriate congressional authorization, defined limits, and a credible plan to transfer responsibilities or bring our personnel home.
statements.context: On her campaign website, on an open-ended ground combat mission abroad

statements.quote: They should have access to every reasonable protection, resource, and tool necessary to keep themselves and our communities safe.
Enforce immigration law, stop trafficking, and put Pennsylvania's security first.
statements.context: On her campaign website home page

researchNotes: Stuski's campaign site discusses several issue areas (food safety, a Pennsylvania regulation, education) in blog posts, but does not state clear stances on any of the guide's fixed issue keys, so no positions are documented for her. Federal key votes and FEC totals for Dean are added separately by script. Issue pages on foreign policy, law enforcement and a platform outline added as statements; no clear stance on the guide's issues beyond these. Dean's official biography says she was raised in Glenside, while Ballotpedia lists Philadelphia as her birthplace; the biography above states only the raised-in detail. Stuski's biography is drawn from her own campaign website; no independent news profile was reviewed.
